data.name: Apsha
data.long_meaning: Apsha is the Sanskrit name of the goddess of water, often depicted as a beautiful woman with a water pot. She is considered the source of all creation and is worshipped for prosperity, purification, and healing. In Hindu mythology, Apsha is the wife of Lord Maruti, the god of wind.

data.cultural_impact: The name Apsha holds significant cultural significance in Hinduism as it represents the goddess of water, who is deeply revered and considered essential for life. She is connected to various rituals, festivals, and belief systems. For instance, in the religious practice of Tirtha Yatra, devotees visit holy rivers or lakes bearing the name of Apsha to gain spiritual purification. Furthermore, the name is invoked during agricultural rituals that seek her blessings for a bountiful harvest.
data.spiritual_significance: Apsha, as a Hindu name, carries immense spiritual significance as it is closely associated with the divine goddess of water. The name resonates with the infinite power and nurturing nature of the divine feminine that provides life-giving sustenance. In Hindu spirituality, water is believed to represent various aspects of the divine, such as cleansing, healing, and purification. By bestowing this name on a child, parents express their hopes for her well-being, prosperity, and spiritual growth. Additionally, the name serves as a constant reminder of the goddess's love, protection, and blessings.

historical_references.reference: The goddess Apshara or Apsha is mentioned in the ancient Indian text the 'Vedas', believed to have been composed between 1500 to 500 BCE. She is described as the wife of the god Mariyaswamy and the mother of the river Goddess Ganga.

The goddess Apsara, an embodiment of sensual pleasure and beauty, is mentioned in Hindu mythology as the celestial dancers and attendants of the gods. They are often depicted as residing in the heavenly abode of Indra.
